events.title: Li Yuan proclaims himself emperor, founding the Tang dynasty
events.description: After the fall of the Sui, Li Yuan took the throne at Chang'an as Emperor Gaozu. The Tang dynasty presided over one of the most brilliant periods of Chinese culture.
events.html: After the fall of the Sui, Li Yuan took the throne at Chang'an as Emperor Gaozu. The Tang dynasty presided over one of the most brilliant periods of Chinese culture.

events.title: A Rus' fleet sails into the Bosphorus and raids Constantinople's suburbs
events.description: A Rus' fleet of about 200 vessels sailed into the Bosphorus and began pillaging the suburbs of Constantinople. It was the only major Rus' expedition recorded in Byzantine and western European sources, and its outcome is unknown in detail.

events.title: Normans rout the army of Pope Leo IX at Civitate
events.description: Normans under Humphrey of Hauteville, Count of Apulia, defeated a Swabian-Italian-Lombard army organised by Pope Leo IX in southern Italy. By 1059 the Normans had allied with the papacy, and Pope Nicholas II recognised their conquest in south Italy.

events.title: Pope Adrian IV crowns Frederick Barbarossa emperor
events.description: For fear of Roman hostility, Pope Adrian IV crowned Frederick Barbarossa emperor secretly on a Saturday instead of the usual Sunday, after a contest over ceremony at their meeting at Sutri. Two years later the word "holy" first appeared with his empire.

events.title: Timur defeats Tokhtamysh at the Kondurcha River
events.description: After a long march across the steppe, Timur defeated his former protégé Tokhtamysh, khan of the Golden Horde, near the Kondurcha River east of present-day Samara. Together with a second defeat on the Terek in 1395, it ruined the Horde.

events.title: Charles VII's army defeats the English at Patay
events.description: The French vanguard, led by La Hire and Jean Poton de Xaintrailles, defeated an English army at Patay, the culmination of the Loire Campaign. The English lost 2,200 men, and John Talbot was among the senior commanders captured.

events.title: United States declares war on Britain
events.description: Madison signed the declaration after Congress narrowly voted for war. The War of 1812 ended in stalemate in 1815, but gave Americans 'The Star-Spangled Banner'.

events.title: Wellington and Blücher defeat Napoleon at Waterloo
events.description: The arrival of Blücher's Prussians broke Napoleon's final assault on Wellington's army near Brussels. Napoleon abdicated four days later and was exiled to St Helena.

events.title: De Gaulle calls on the French to fight on
events.description: Speaking on the BBC from London, General Charles de Gaulle rejected the coming armistice and urged French forces to continue resistance. The appeal founded the Free French movement.

events.title: Carter and Brezhnev sign the SALT II treaty
events.description: The treaty capped each side's strategic nuclear launchers. The US Senate never ratified it after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, though both sides largely observed its limits.
